title: Rob Lowe’s Daily Wire drama splits critics: ‘Masterpiece’ or ‘Tedious’?

 Rob Lowe’s Daily Wire drama Confession splits critics: ‘Masterpiece’ or ‘Tedious’?
 The movie, with a script by Ben Shapiro, also stars James Franco and Jennifer Jason Leigh
 Kevin E G Perry in Los Angeles Thursday 12 November 2026 13:21 EST

 The new Daily Wire -produced drama Confession has divided critics, with some tepid on the film while others are hailing it as “masterpiece.”
 The movie, directed by Václav Marhoul and the first to be written by conservative podcaster Ben Shapiro , is set in Moscow in 1938 during the era of Stalin’s political purges.
 It stars Rob Lowe as Alexei , an alcoholic literature professor who is accused of conspiring with a priest who has been critical of the Soviet regime. James Franco also stars as Vladimir, a former pupil of Alexei and now his ruthless interrogator.
 For The Hollywood Reporter ’s Frank Scheck, the result proves a “dull, turgid slog.”
 “Hopelessly stilted in its execution (it’s the kind of prison drama in which the guards and soldiers speak with all the realism of automatons), the terminally tedious Confession seems mainly designed to demonstrate that its screenwriter benefited from a really good education during which he studied all the Russian literary masters,” argues Scheck.
 Rob Lowe stars in the controversial Daily Wire drama 'Confession' ( The Daily Wire ) Variety ’s Joe Leydon took a similar view, writing that Confession feels “talky and sluggish.”
 Leydon added: “Lead actors Rob Lowe and James Franco do a credible and creditable job of inhabiting their characters, and somehow manage to strike potent emotional sparks with even the more stilted dialogue.”
 Conservative news site The Free Press was much more positive, with critic Rod Dreher heralding the film as a “masterpiece.”
 Dreher goes on to praise Confession as “extraordinary,” arguing that it tackles weighty questions about faith and truth and praising Franco for his performance “with the eyes and delivery of a spitting cobra.”
 Sasha Stone of Awards Daily was similarly impressed, calling the film a “great leap forward” for The Daily Wire .
 “In a better culture, one not captured by a totalitarian worldview, Shaprio’s screenplay, along with the performances in this film, would be considered for the Oscars,” claimed Stone.
 Rebecca Onion, of Slate , found something to love in the performances if not the movie at large, writing: “It’s a real tribute to the craft of the professional actor that such a darkly lit, visually boring movie could be at all watchable.”
 While Onion says the film can be “tedious stuff,” she goes on to make her “own confession: Despite the canned feeling of the script and the monotony of the direction, I enjoyed seeing Franco on screen again. Broadened out in middle age after his years out of the spotlight, he uses his shifty eyes and shit-eating grin to good purpose in playing Vladimir.”
 Confession is streaming on DailyWire+.
